s001: FluxBio: open-source Link in bio + short links
s002: An open-source Link-in-bio and short link tool that runs on Cloudflare Workers. Buttons on your page show the real address and still count clicks, or use a short link at the flip of a switch. Connect your AI, and updating your page or checking your stats is as easy as asking.

s051: Build your page, share your links and see what works, all in one dashboard. Only want short links? Turn pages off.
s052: Each of the 24 themes has its own design and a few color sets to pick from. Want your own pictures and colors? Have your AI make one for you.
s053: Buttons on your page show the real address, so visitors can see where they go. Every link also has a short link, ready under Share, and one switch puts it on the button for links you’d rather not show, like affiliate links. You can make standalone ones too, with your own slug in any language, Thai and Hindi included.
s054: See the clicks on every link button and where visitors came from, like IG, Threads or LINE, so you know what to push in your next post. You choose whether social icons count too. Buttons showing the real address are counted by a tiny script on the page, so a blocker can hide a click; short links always count.
s055: Create a token in the dashboard and paste the prompt into Claude Code, Codex or Cursor. Domain, time zone, backups, a whole batch of short links: no menus to dig through. FluxBio’s guide tells your AI to say what will be affected before it publishes, deletes anything or changes a URL.

s062: FluxBio is free and open source. It runs on your own Cloudflare account, whose free plan covers ten thousand to several tens of thousands of page views a day, depending on the pictures on your page (try the estimate above), and several hundred changes. That’s usually more than individuals and small shops need. Subscriptions to AIs like Claude or ChatGPT are separate, and Claude Code needs a paid Claude plan.
s063: Everything lives in your own Cloudflare account: pages, short links and stats in D1, images in KV. FluxBio has no central server, and its author can’t see your data. Published pages and short links are public. Drafts are visible only to you and anyone with a preview link, and stats and the dashboard need a sign-in.
s064: The dashboard password is how you sign in to the dashboard. It’s made for you when you deploy, and you can change it anytime. API tokens are for AIs and tools: give each AI its own, limit one to creating short links if you like, and revoke any of them without affecting the rest. Cloudflare credentials are for what only Cloudflare can do, like deploying or connecting a domain. They control your whole Cloudflare account, so never paste them into a chat.
s065: Revoke that token under Settings in the dashboard and make a new one. Your other AIs keep working. If your dashboard password leaks, ask your AI to change it: everyone gets signed out, and every token stops working too.
s066: Page edits go to a draft, and visitors see nothing until it’s published. Settings and standalone short links change at once. FluxBio’s guide tells your AI to explain what will change and ask you first, to ask whether to publish straight away or preview first, and to save a backup before it starts. If something goes wrong, it can put back one of a page’s last 20 published versions, or restore a backup. A tool that doesn’t read the guide won’t do any of this, so only give full access to an AI you trust.
s067: Yes. Editing pages, changing the look, making short links and QR codes, checking stats and downloading backups all happen in the dashboard. Settings like the domain and time zone, and a look with your own colors and pictures, have no screen and are changed through the API: every FluxBio explains how at /llms.txt.
s068: To deploy: we recommend Claude Code on your own computer. Other coding agents that can run commands with internet access work too, such as Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, Cline, Roo Code, Kilo Code, Droid, Crush, Goose, Pi, TRAE, Qoder, ZCode, Eigent, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot or Windsurf. To run your site day to day: those, plus anything that can call an API, such as the Claude app, Claude Cowork, ChatGPT (custom GPTs) or n8n. Settings in the dashboard gives you a prompt to paste into Claude Code, Codex or Cursor; for anything else, point it at your site’s /llms.txt.
s069: Just ask your AI: “Switch the domain to links.example.com”, “Change my dashboard password”, “Move my site to another FluxBio”. A new domain first has to be connected to this Worker in Cloudflare, and your AI will walk you through it.
s070: FluxBio uses no cookies and stores no IP addresses or full user-agent strings. For each visit it keeps the time, where the visitor came from, their device, browser, language, network and rough location (about 10 km at best) for 90 days, with a one-way hash that changes every day. Totals are kept for good. Known bots and link previews don’t count. Two things do reach Google: fonts load from Google Fonts unless you turn that off under Appearance, and a page with a YouTube video loads its thumbnail from there.

s148: What happens if I use up the free plan? Will I be charged?
s149: You won’t be charged. The free plan needs no card. If a day’s allowance runs out, visitors see an error until it starts over at midnight UTC. If your AI runs on your computer, it can tell you how much is left today.
s150: My AI keeps asking if it can run things. What do I press?
s151: That’s normal: it asks before it does anything on your computer. If it’s downloading FluxBio, installing tools or deploying, allow it. If you don’t follow what it wants to do, ask it to explain first.
s152: Is my site still there when I turn off my computer? How do I change it tomorrow?
s153: Once it’s online, yes. Your site lives on Cloudflare, not on your computer. To change it, open your AI tool and say what you want, for example “Add my YouTube channel to my FluxBio page”. Claude Code remembers your site; in other tools, paste the prompt from Settings again.
s154: Do I need my own domain?
s155: No. You get a free workers.dev address that works once it’s deployed and doesn’t expire. It’s just longer. If you later have a domain on Cloudflare, you can add it, and links you’ve already shared keep working.
s156: What if I try it and don’t want it?
s157: You can just leave it: it costs nothing. To remove everything, tell your AI “Delete my whole FluxBio”. It offers to save a backup and checks with you before deleting anything.
s158: Can I use it without a Link-in-bio page?
s159: Yes. Any page can be your own HTML or redirect to another address, and either can be your home page: ask your AI, or choose on the page’s Content tab. You can also switch pages off and use only short links.
s160: Stats cover the last 7, 30 or 90 days. A backup holds your pages, short links, images and settings, but not click history, API tokens or publish history.
s161: Can I try it without a Cloudflare account?
s162: Yes. Your AI makes a sample page on your computer, with no account at all. Its address only opens on your computer, so you can’t send it to a friend, and after a restart you ask your AI to open it again, with nothing lost. When you’re happy, get a free Cloudflare account to put it online, and what you made comes along. If you’d rather not, ask your AI to delete the folder.
s163: How much traffic does the free plan cover?
s164: Say your Cloudflare account holds FluxBio alone. Put in the traffic you expect and see whether the free plan covers it, and if not, what Workers Paid costs a month.
s165: With the defaults (5 pictures on a page, three in ten visitors tapping a link, every visitor new), the free plan covers about 15,000 page views a day, and more the more people come back. Workers Paid is US$5 a month and includes about 1.5 million page views.
s173: 5 by default: a profile picture, a cover and a background, plus the gallery or product pictures in view when the page opens. Pictures further down load only when scrolled to, and a returning visitor's browser already has them, so the real number is usually lower.
